//verify_after_merge: Build the Lean project and run tools/print_axioms.sh after every merge, and refuse to record a target as done if either fails. The driver used to call a target done on the agent's own say-so without compiling a line. Takes about half a minute on a warm cache against runs of several hours.
//stop_after_idle_continues: How many continuations that change no .lean file to allow before calling a target finished. Aristotle reports a partial status for a pass that found nothing to repair just as it does for one cut off mid-proof, so without this a finished target is re-submitted until its budget is gone. 0 disables continuations entirely; a high number restores the old behaviour.
//pause_on: Conditions that halt the queue outright rather than just filing a review item. Options: failed, partial. Audits and still-open results always file an item and never halt, so a week away does not stall on the first surprise.
standing_instructions:
---
Standing rules for this run (they apply to every task in this series; do not treat them as part of the mathematical goal):

* Work only inside `transducer-lean/`. Do not modify the LaTeX sources of the book.
* Never weaken, generalise away or delete the statement of a numbered result in order to make it provable, and never close a goal with `sorry`, with a new `axiom`, or with `native_decide`. If a statement of the book is false as literally written, or needs an extra hypothesis, then keep a faithful rendering, add the corrected version next to it, and document the discrepancy both in the docstring and in `THEOREMS.md` -- exactly as was already done for Definition A.2.7, for the derivative used in Lemma A.2.10, and for Theorem B.4.6.
* Prefer reusing the machinery that is already in the project over rebuilding it; the existing files are listed in `THEOREMS.md`.
* `lake build` must succeed with no errors at the end of the task. Leave the repository building even if you are interrupted.
* For every numbered result you finish, run `#print axioms` on it and confirm it depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Record that in `THEOREMS.md`.
* Before finishing, update `THEOREMS.md`: the status column of every result you touched, the list of files, and the `## Status` section. Then commit.
* In your closing summary, state plainly which numbered results are now proved outright, which are proved from an explicit hypothesis (and which hypothesis), and which are still open with what remains to be done. Do not describe a result as proved if any of its dependencies still contains `sorry`.
* A result proved from an explicit hypothesis is not proved. Do not introduce a new `def ... : Prop` and take it as an argument in order to close a goal, unless the task you were given says in so many words that you may; and never trade one assumption for another that is no weaker. If you do add one, say so in your summary in the same breath as the theorem it supports, and record it in `THEOREMS.md` or `EXERCISES.md` with the reason.
* Theorem C.4.17 has been withdrawn from this formalisation by the author of the book: the book does not prove it. It is not an open result, it must not be reinstated or counted as missing, and if you still find its statement in the sources then removing it is the right thing to do.
* Identify a result of the book by its LaTeX `\label`, not by its number. Numbers move whenever the book is edited -- a result inserted earlier renumbers everything after it -- and a docstring or a table that names one silently becomes wrong. The label does not move, and the number can always be recovered from it through `main.aux`, whereas the label cannot be recovered from the number. So write `Theorem `thm:mso-logic-languages`` rather than `Theorem C.4.1`, in docstrings and in `THEOREMS.md` alike.
* Your copy of the book is older than the author's and does not have every label. If you cannot find a result's `\label` in the sources you have, say so plainly in your summary and leave the number in place for that one result -- do not invent a label, and do not guess it from the file name.
* `EXERCISES.md` and `RequestProject/Exercises.lean` are assembled from the work of several runs. Add your own chapter's section and your own imports to them; do not rewrite either file wholesale, and leave other chapters' entries exactly as you found them, even if you would have written them differently. Two runs that each rewrite an index file collide on it every time.
* Questions are disabled in this run: if something is ambiguous, make a reasonable choice, document it in the docstring, and continue.
